I2.quote: Nanoporous carbon were fabricated by controlled pyrolysis of ground corncob using a proprietary multi-step method [6]. All samples under consideration in this paper were prepared in granular form.

I5.quote: It is shown how appropriately engineered nanoporous carbons provide materials for reversible hydrogen storage, based on physisorption, with exceptional storage capacities (∼80 g H2 /kg carbon, ∼50 g H2 /liter carbon, at 50 bar and 77 K).

notes: PDF page 1 is an IOPscience download cover sheet; locations give the PDF page and the journal's printed page. Section 7 calls Table 5 'A list of our typical BET surface areas', but Table 5 ('Specific surface areas of samples') gives N2 BET (0.01-0.03 p/p0) and NLDFT areas for the two measured samples, Batch 5.1 and S-33/k, so this is a sample-specific value, not a value typical of a kind of material. Table 1 footnote a marks only the S-33/k Hiden IGA-001 values as extrapolated from isotherms; the S-33/k U. Missouri value at 77 K, 50 bar carries no footnote, and Figure 1 shows measured excess isotherms. Reference [6], a US patent application, describes the synthesis only; this document is a primary research article. No retraction notice and no statement that the H2 uptake values were published before.
